MADSWIMMERS Swimming for Climate Change

By: Diana Lucas | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Currently, the world’s highest Lake is at 5,930 metres above sea level (masl) and the highest body of water is at 6,400 masl.

The Himalayas currently host the second highest lake in the world. Ojos del Salado the volcanic crater lake in Argentina is the highest. But as the planet warms up more lakes are being created at even higher altitudes. Reports from sherpas on Mount Everest say there is a new lake in the Himalayas a higher one created by climate change. If they are right this is the highest body of water in the world. Its meant to be somewhere on Putha Hiunchuli (Himalayas) which stands at 7,246 metres above sea level.

Six ‘mad’ swimmers, from different countries and backgrounds, are going to attempt to reach this body of water and then swim it. These are ‘ordinary people’, some with no mountaineering or extreme swimming experience. Call them irresponsible danger freaks but this an expedition led by Jean Craven, of Madswimmers, South Africa. What they do is extreme physical feats to raise money for charities.


Further information:
This is a world record to break, swimming at the top of the world. The team’ physical well being will hinge on their differences and diversity which will make of break the expedition.
This world record challenge is a team effort to create more awareness and interest for what is happening to the planet. At the same time, it will show how a diverse community can come together and survive when pushing medical boundaries in extreme cold and with very little oxygen.

Script:


V/O
The vision was an ambitious high altitude record attempt

V/O
Few if any of those taking part, fully understood the arduous challenge that lay ahead

V/0
A trek that would push them to their limits

Up Sound: I feel completely out of my comfort zone
Up Sound: There’s some snow more than expected
Up Sound: Slowly the expedition is moving forward


Sean: People said we were crazy
Jean: We had to do something WOW, that’s mad.

Link
This team had a single minded vision. The highest swim in the world
And its here in Kathmandu it all began

V/O
Kathmandu, Nepal, a city where mountaineers and adventures pour in every spring, at the start of the three, month window, to scale the Himalaya’s highest peaks.
It’s here we meet Jean Craven - a man with a passion for swimming,

V/O
Jean started the ‘Madswimmer’ charity in 2009.

Jean It’s always been an open charity driven association, anyone can come and join us for swims, I guess the only pre requisite is you must be able to swim. so over the years its grown we have an excess of 400 swimmers joined us in the last 15 years. from 30 different countries.

V/O
In 2015 Carte Blanche met up with the Madswimmers - in the Andes Mountains, in South America where they set a new world record, the highest altitude swim at 5 900 metres.

But Just over a year later that record was broken – again in the Andes- when an Australian – Dan Bull swam higher at 6 370 metres above sea level.

Jean I was reading about his swim and I said you know what Australians can’t take the record from a South African-
Mac: Not the Aussies.
Jean: And that was four years ago- and we have got to get that back.
Mac Who was crazy enough to come with you on this Mad swim
Jean: Fortunately, I met another crazy South African Sean Disney. Sean was the man who took us to that lake when we broke the first altitude record

Sean: Jean came to me and said Sean we need to swim higher, we need to get this record back. I said Jean there is no higher lake let me sleep on it.

V/O
It took a while before Sean Disney - two-time Everest summiteer and two-time 7 Summits climber, came up with a plan, to swim in the mighty Himalayas.

Sean: It was a hassle it wasn’t easy. we were heading out into unchartered territory.

V/O
Getting a permit to actually swim in the mountains of Nepal was a complicated and long process of negotiation.

Sean: We were originally swimming on Mount Everest on Camp 2 but the Nepalese Government declined that so they put us in the back corner of Nepal said go do your thing we are not quiet sure what you are doing. and that’s how we headed out to Mt Putcha in the middle of nowhere.

V/O
The swimmers who joined Jean to swim, higher than anyone has done before, were for the most part ordinary people, with no climbing experience.

Vanes: Cool I am going to go and hike and I have never hiked before I am going to swim I have never swum in ice water

V/O
TV Presenter, Vanes- Marie Du Toit,

…and I am going to do that for a month and hopefully get something positive out of it.

Neo: I am open to challenges I want to do something difficult to show people the possibilities of like the human spirit,

V/O
Filmmaker Neo Kunene

Neo: I was like sign me up.

V/O
They were joined by an experienced swimmer from Turkey, a doctor and a cameraman.

Visuals Team in Kathmandu

Link: Ok so Gloves check, jacket check, crampons check but no matter how much equipment you get nothing could prepare these guys for what they were about to face.

Vanes: Mac it was so intimidating when we went into the gear shop and it was ok Vanes you need snow boots Harness’s, ice axe. You need an ice axe we’re from South Africa.
Neo: They kept mentioning, guys, things never go according to plan, what you think you have planned cut it out of your mind and whatever happens happens.

V/O
After a short flight into Nepalgunj, first step of their journey was a nerve wracking 17 hour jeep ride to Denai.

Deniz: The most hectic drive of my life,
Neo: That ride was the scariest drive we have ever been on…we were driving past cliffs and all that stuff…

V/O
In Dunai the Madswimmers were joined by 21 sherpas and a caravan of donkeys before they embarked on q 138 kilometre trek that would take them to the peaks of the Himalayas and hopefully an ice cold dip.

Vanes: I think initially it was just kind of absorbing everything and taking in sounds and smells and the beautiful nature. And I have this funny thing in my mind people say go hike and enjoy the nature but all you hear is …. BREATHES

Visuals huffing and puffing

Sean: Every day was like a surprise. These guys are swimmers not climbers.
Mac: How hard was it for you to get them safely to the top?
Sean: You know Jean has experience in the mountains but the rest of them haven’t it’s like starting from scratch. Every day was touch and go, I couldn’t tell you if we would make or not.

Jean sound up ‘3 000 metres done and dusted’.

V/O
The MAD swimmers mission is to raise money for charities and passing through the last village on Mt Putha they spread a little of their madswimmer magic.

Neo: It was a really touching moment we always take for granted the little things. Like just the jacket to them it means the world to them?

V/O
Donkeys can only go so high. Over 3 000 metres the Yaks took over.

Jean: We need about 30 to 35 Yaks to take us up there in the snow. Donkeys ain’t going to work.
Mac: Were there any life threatening moments?
Jean: I am generally a bok for sports but we started ascending and the only route to our base camp was across this monster of a mountain and I remember asking our Sherpa so how do we get across that and he said no we are just going to go over the top. I said can a Yak go over there he sais no, and I got a bit worried.

Vanes: Those moments of what the hell am I doing, I have a size 9 shoe right? Putting my feet next to each other I am already taking up a lot of space. if you are on top of the mountain and the ridge is as narrow as 2 feet next to each other. It’s like two, three kilometres down. I remember my walking stick going and I touched a rock and the rock started going down and I looked at the rock and I thought please do not let that be me today.

Jean: Listen I have done a bridge swim and jumped out of a plane with a parachute but this was next level.

V/O
On the 10th day of their gruelling, upward ascent the team reached Mt Putha Base camp.

Jean: The sherpas wont go up with peace if the ceremony is not done. I like this Buddhist ceremony that ends up with a tot of vodka but it was very special I must say.

Jean: The oxygen levels drop drastically the higher you go, Mad swimmers has always been around we team and not I so you have got team pressure.
Mac: But you also have to come face to face with yourself?
Jean: Those last 2 days just before we hit Camp 2 was one of my toughest days. It was a 400 metre climb mostly with crampons, we had a fixed line, it was snowing, the weather was bad…I was just hoping my team would get there. It was digging deep.

V/O
And then the really MAD part, the swimmers passed the last body of water at 5 900 metres, not high enough to set a new world record. For the highest swim the team had to create their own pool.

Vanes: I am cold and can’t breathe. Every thing you see is just mountain ranges and then you look to the right and there is this little ice pool waiting for you.
Neo: I’m pumped psyched ready to break the world record with the mad swimmers.
Sean: When I saw these guys coming out in their SA speedo I was sitting there with my amazing team of 21 sherpas we just watched in awe we knew we had pulled it off.

Vanes: In the highest, most expensive pool in the world.

Jean: We swam in 3.7 which is chilly, three minutes not too long, but with sun on your back and having had three weeks of pain getting to this height, it was bliss.

V/O
An expedition of unexpected twists and turns comes to an end. … the Mad swimmers aren’t experienced climbers, but undeterred they struggled through the harsh 15-day ascent to complete their mission: a swim at the highest ever altitude. But, as is so often the case, this was about the journey more than the destination. And we leave inspired by a team that embraced an unexpected test of their courage… all in the name of charity.

Mac: Would you say this swim was the easiest part of this whole challenge?
Jean It was but to get there…I want to say to next guy who wants to try record, `Good Luck

Visuals

Promo 1 21 sec

V/O
Four swimmers attempt to create a new world record.
Jean I said you no what an Australian can’t take that.
Mac: Not the Aussies
Jean And, that’s where it all started Gotta get that back
V/O
After 15 days of gruelling hiking and climbing in the Himalayan mountains
Vanes: Those moments of what the hell am I doing.
V/O
Will they swim higher than anyone has done before.


Promo 2 21 secs

The Madswimmers have spent the last 15 years taking on outrageous and challenging swims
Up Sounds
From High up in the Andes ……
……to the Dead Sea,
Creating new world records and raising money for charities swim by swim

Promo 3 21 secs

V/O
The Sky’s the limit for this group of Mad swimmers
Jean : Raising funds for charity you really have to go the extra mile and doing something WOW
V/O
Who attempt a new world record, the highest swim in the world.
Sean: People said we were crazy
Vanes: It is amazing…in the highest most expensive swimming pool in the world

metadata.Summary: Currently, the world’s highest Lake is at 5,930 metres above sea level (masl) and the highest body of water is at 6,400 masl. The Himalayas currently host the second highest lake in the world. Ojos del Salado the volcanic crater lake in Argentina is the highest. But as the planet warms up more lakes are being created at even higher altitudes. Reports from sherpas on Mount Everest say there is a new lake in the Himalayas a higher one created by climate change. If they are right this is the highest body of water in the world. Its meant to be somewhere on Putha Hiunchuli (Himalayas) which stands at 7,246 metres above sea level. Six ‘mad’ swimmers, from different countries and backgrounds, are going to attempt to reach this body of water and then swim it. These are ‘ordinary people’, some with no mountaineering or extreme swimming experience. Call them irresponsible danger freaks but this an expedition led by Jean Craven, of Madswimmers, South Africa. What they do is extreme physical feats to raise money for charities.
metadata.Further information: This is a world record to break, swimming at the top of the world. The team’ physical well being will hinge on their differences and diversity which will make of break the expedition. This world record challenge is a team effort to create more awareness and interest for what is happening to the planet. At the same time, it will show how a diverse community can come together and survive when pushing medical boundaries in extreme cold and with very little oxygen.
